interpretation: The selected head does not achieve perfect TRAIN binary decisions with its frozen served thresholds. Nearly all missed TRAIN decisions nevertheless have correct categorical argmax values for all six fields.
The served coupled-policy score is a function of full probabilities and fitted pair potentials, so categorical correctness does not imply that the score clears its saved threshold.
There are12 joint-field TRAIN errors versus1433 joint-field DEV errors on populations with different compositions. Larger model capacity alone is not established as the missing ingredient.

The existing objective trains separate binary cross-entropy and class-weighted field cross-entropy, plus teacher KL. It does not directly optimize cross-entropy of the coupled-policy score selected for serving. This objective/serving difference motivates a prospective consistency-loss experiment; it does not prove a cause or that such a loss will improve any gate.
next_experiment_hypothesis: A separately registered small-head experiment could add a differentiable loss for the served coupled-policy probability while retaining field supervision, data splits, initial weights and strict qualification gates. First verify analytic probabilities and gradients against independent references. No threshold is changed by this audit.
